I have created [filter.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py) (mounted at `/app/filter.py` in the container) to sanitize HTML files in-place and prevent XSS attacks while preserving original HTML structure and formatting.

### Key Capabilities
- **In-Place CLI Execution**: Reads the target HTML file from `sys.argv[1]` (`[`main`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L1167-L1185)`) and writes the sanitized content back in-place while preserving file encoding and newline formatting.
- **Formatting-Preserving HTML5 Sanitization**:
  - [`sanitize_html`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L1155-L1164) and [`sanitize_html_once`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L827-L1129) scan the document using HTML5 tokenization rules to excise only harmful tags, attributes, and declarations without altering indentation, whitespace, attribute ordering, quote styles, or void tag syntax.
  - Removes active/executable elements (`<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<frame>`, `<frameset>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<applet>`, `<base>`, SVG SMIL animation tags `<animate*>`, `<set>`, `<handler>`, `<foreignObject>`, `<use>`, dangerous `<meta>`/`<link>` tags, and empty XSS `<svg>`/`<math>` shells) and runs until fixed-point convergence to defeat nested tag reconstruction (`<scr<script>ipt>`).
  - [`reconstruct_start_tag`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L752-L824) and [`is_dangerous_attribute`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L340-L423) strip all `on*` event handlers, `srcdoc`, and obfuscated `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, and dangerous `data:` URIs (handling numeric/hex/named HTML entities with or without semicolons, control characters, whitespace, and URL/CSS escapes).
  - [`sanitize_inline_style`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L263-L303) and [`sanitize_style_block`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-vxa7n0l4/filter.py#L306-L337) preserve safe CSS rules while removing `expression(...)`, `javascript:`/`vbscript:` URLs, `@import`, `-moz-binding`, and `behavior:` declarations.
